items.q: What is the German word for 'Christmas'?
items.why: Students struggle with Weihnachten spelling - the 'ei' and 'ch' and double 'a' confuse. Also it grammatically behaves as a plural noun (zu Weihnachten = at Christmas). Other festival terms: Ostern (Easter), Silvester (New Year's Eve).

items.q: How do you say 'my sister' in German?
items.why: Students forget possessive endings. Possessives (mein, dein, sein, ihr, unser, euer) take the SAME ENDINGS as ein/eine. Schwester is feminine = meine. Mein Bruder (masc), meine Schwester (fem), mein Kind (neut), meine Eltern (pl).

items.q: What is the gender of 'Lieblingsfach' (favourite subject)?
items.why: Students think the first word determines gender. In compound nouns, the LAST element determines the gender. Fach is neuter, so das Lieblingsfach. Same rule: das Lieblingsbuch (das Buch), die Lieblingsfarbe (die Farbe).

items.q: Which sentence correctly says 'I get on well with my mother'?
items.correct: Ich verstehe mich gut mit meiner Mutter.
items.misconception: Ich verstehe mich gut mit meine Mutter.
items.random_wrong: Ich verstehe mir gut mit meiner Mutter.
items.why: Correct answer: Ich verstehe mich gut mit meiner Mutter.. “Ich verstehe mich gut mit meine Mutter.” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: Which form of 'you' do you use addressing a German teacher?
items.why: Correct answer: Sie. “du” sounds right because it borrows the language of the topic — but it fails this question. Re-read the notes on why.

items.q: How many grammatical cases does standard German have?
items.why: Exact answer: 4 cases. Estimation gets you near it; only the anchored number survives the exam hall.
